sections.overview: This Colombian frog was originally described as Eleutherodactylus xylochobates and is now placed in Pristimantis. The original description identifies P. cacao and P. chrysops as its closest relatives.
sections.identification: The regional species account describes adults as reddish brown, with a smooth back; compared with P. chrysops, they are smaller and lack heel tubercles and labial stripes.
sections.habitat: It is known from the high crest of the Serranía de los Paraguas, in cloud-forest country of western Colombia.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet details were not found in the consulted accounts.
sections.behavior: The consulted species accounts provide no specific behavioral observations.
sections.reproduction: The consulted species accounts provide no species-specific reproductive details.
sections.ecology: Its known range is exceptionally restricted: the global threatened-amphibian account reported only two localities along this mountain crest.
sections.conservation: A global threatened-amphibian account classified it as Vulnerable. Colombia’s 2024 national threatened-species list places it in Critically Endangered.
